transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit
From what you have described, the most likely cause is the automatic defrost system. Behind the rear panel inside the freezer, are the coils a solid block of ice, or fairly clear?
not sure, never taken a panel off. its a manual defrost freezer tho, i just defrost it myself. ice is mostly round the front edge and bottom drawer

From what you have described, the most likely cause is a blocked defrost drain. Ice in the bottom often means the defrost water can't drain away. At the bottom of the back wall there's a small drain hole — once the ice has melted, clear it gently with warm water or a soft pipe cleaner. Was the drain hole blocked (and is it clear now), is it still blocked or frozen, or was it already clear?
haven't checked the drain yet. but the freezer door doesn't feel like it seals properly, ice is worst by the door edge. what should i check?

Run your fingers round the rubber seal on the door and look for splits, gaps or a section that has come away, especially where the frost is. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
just looked, bottom corner of the freezer door seal is split about 5cm and the hinge-side bottom bit is flattened. kids yank that drawer so prob them. can i replace the seal myself?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Yes, replacing a freezer door seal is usually a manageable DIY job with basic tools, as on most fridge-freezers it either pushes into a channel or is held by screws under the rubber edge. The main thing is getting the exact seal for your model, as they're made to fit specific doors. The checks point to the door seal. To find the right part, could you give me the model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the fridge, usually on a side wall near the salad drawer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its an Indesit, model IB55532W off the rating plate. is the seal push-in or screwed? not sure till i look closer

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
I can't confirm which type your IB55532W uses, because the model isn't matched in our parts catalogue. Fridge-freezer door seals are usually either push-in (pressed into a groove in the door liner) or held by screws under the seal lip. The checks point to the door seal. I could not find a confirmed match for model IB55532W in our parts catalogue, so check with the manufacturer or a parts supplier using the full model number, or ask an appliance engineer to fit it.
